A good bond for the new Bond? Zendaya, Jodie Comer and Sydney Sweeney

After months of speculation, we finally have a new Bond. The question now is - who will play Robert Pattinson’s leading lady?

What’s clear is that Pattinson’s announcement as 007 has completely upped the game.

He's one of Hollywood's biggest stars, so all eyes are on Amazon MGM to see whether they also go for an equally big name for a "Bond girl", or if they'll take a chance on someone a little less well known.

Whoever is cast opposite him, though, needs to have a "very strong identity of her own", believes film critic Larushka Ivan-Zadeh - "someone distinctive, sexy, complicated".

Showbiz reporter Catrina Rose agrees: "I'd love to see a Bond girl who's just as interesting and unpredictable as he is."

And then, some say the whole concept of a Bond girl is outdated and the role needs to evolve for a new era. So what can we expect?

No actress has yet confirmed they're in the running - but stars who have been bandied about the internet include Zendaya , whose name shot to the top of the list after Pattinson's casting.

The duo have already shared three films together this year, and make a "really exciting pairing," says Ivan-Zadeh.

Rose agrees that as one of the most recognisable actresses in Hollywood, Zendaya is "definitely someone I'd be thinking about now".

But her Euphoria co-stars Hunter Schafer and Sydney Sweeney could give her a run for her money.

There have been rumours about Sweeney getting the role for months, and you can see why, says Dr Llewella Chapman, a film historian at the University of East Anglia. "She has sex appeal and an ability to take on tougher roles too," she tells the BBC.

Sweeney was given a boost last month by former Bond girl Trina Parks, who told the Telegraph she would fit the role well because Bond needed a woman with "ownership over her sexuality".

Robert Pattinson said "to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime"

Speculation is also growing over Pattinson’s partner, actor and singer Suki Waterhouse . She once said she’d love to play , external " a bad-ass Bond girl , external ".

But there isn’t a precedent for husband-wife couples in the films, and it may be more likely that she picks up a cameo role, if indeed she wants to.

Meanwhile, TV presenter Maya Jama has picked up new interest following her storming run on Celebrity Traitors. After she quit Love Island , rumours swirled that she could be the next Bond girl - but she’s just signed a Netflix deal, so it’s unclear if that would still be a possibility.

Another strong contender is Florence Pugh who, like Zendaya, also stars alongside Pattinson in Dune: Part Three. Earlier this week she threw her hat in the ring to be in the new Bond film - although as a villain, rather than his leading lady.

"She ticks quite a few boxes if they're looking for someone bankable," says Rose. "I could absolutely see her as a Bond woman who turns out to be the villain, someone Bond thinks is on his side, but she's actually been playing him the whole time."

Florence Pugh stars alongside Robert Pattinson in Dune: Part Three, reprising her role as Princess Irulan

Queen's Gambit star Anya Taylor-Joy is another name Amazon MGM could be thinking about if they want a big, recognisable actress, as well as Killing Eve's Jodie Comer (Villanelle meets Bond, anyone?)

Meanwhile, Crazy Rich Asians star Gemma Chan told Variety she was "flattered" by fans speculating she could be a Bond girl. "Absolutely I would," she said , external .

Other names that have been floated include Saoirse Ronan, Margaret Qualley, Marisa Abela, Emily Blunt, Lily James, Chase Infiniti, Inde Navarrette, Simone Ashley, Deva Cassel and Ambika Mod .

And it could easily be someone totally different. Producers have previously chosen a Bond girl who isn't particularly famous yet - or is on the cusp of stardom.

Monica Bellucci made history as the oldest "Bond girl" in the franchise when she portrayed Lucia Sciarra in Spectre

But then there’s the wider question of whether the whole idea of a “Bond girl” is now somewhat outdated.

Historically, the character had little agency and existed primarily as Bond's romantic interest - and the term "girl" itself is also criticised for infantilising women.

Monica Bellucci rejected the label. She told the Guardian , external ahead of her appearance in Sceptre in 2015: "I can't say I'm a Bond girl because I'm too mature to be a Bond girl. I say Bond lady; Bond woman."

The way the films have treated Bond girls "hasn't always aged well", says Rose.

Some scenes from 1960s Bond films are "basically rape", and "wouldn't fly today", said No Time To Die director Cary Fukunaga in 2021 , external - referring to Thunderball and Goldfinger.

In reality, we have come a long way since then.

Over the years, producers have taken steps to usher the franchise into the modern era.

These days, the women of Bond are now much more likely to be sharp, capable equals to 007 - and what's defined as "attractive" has also evolved.

Belluci's inclusion in Spectre as a "Bond woman" aged 50 was widely praised for spotlighting a different type of sex appeal (even though she was only four years older than Daniel Craig in real life).

We've also had other powerful women in Bond, such as Michelle Yeoh's Colonel Wai Lin and Lashana Lynch's MI6 agent Nomi, who also made history as the first black female 007 .

Rather than fitting the traditional Bond girl mould, both of them were competent women who could give Bond a run for his money.

"We've moved away from the role being someone with a silly name and for Bond to pat on their bottom," says film critic Ivan-Zadeh. "It's moving in the right direction".

Many people say, however, there is still further to go.

Having more female Bond villains, as well as love interests, could be one way to make it more equal, suggests Rose. "That's what I'd want to see."

"They can be romantic interests, villains, spies, allies or even the person who ultimately outsmarts Bond. There's room for all of those roles,” agrees showbiz journalist Nikki Onafuye.

Another way the roles could evolve is by bringing in "a queer or sexually fluid Bond woman," says Ivan-Zadeh. "Someone whose desires don’t simply revolve around Bond. That would create some genuinely interesting chemistry.”

Others are hoping to see more diverse actresses cast from film markets such as China, India or Nigeria.

“There have been a number of women of colour in the past, but I'd like to see more," says Be Manzini, writer and film-maker.

"I'd like to see an Indian Bond girl," agrees Chapman. "Aishwarya Rai was touted for the follow up to Die Another Day but never got there."

More broadly, there is an appetite to see Bond girls have their own lives.

“For me, it's about giving these women proper storylines,” says Onafuye. "They should have their own motivations and their own ambitions.”

None of this is to say we should do away with the traditional Bond glamour.

"No-one wants to see Bond girls slumping around in their PJs," says Ivan-Zadeh.

But the important distinction is that "being sexy shouldn't be the only thing a female character has to offer,” says Onafuye.

“To those arguing that it's fine for Bond's women just to be sexy and hot, I'd say there's nothing sexier or hotter than a woman (or man) with a brain and a wit,” adds entertainment journalist Caroline Frost.

Aishwarya Rai's name appears in Indian tabloids whenever a new 007 film enters pre-production

Ultimately, whatever direction the new producers go in, most agree the "Bond girl" or Bond woman is a key part of the Bond universe.

But continuing to evolve is crucial, says Chapman. "It's about retaining the humour and history of Bond but also recognising - this is 2026."

There are, of course, lots of other women within the films, and for Frost, the key is to have a range of different Bond women on screen, "all well matched with 007 in terms of strength, resources and, above all, wit".

"Bond has always had fascinating women," agrees Rose. "I'd just love the next film to give them the space to be as interesting as the man in the tuxedo."

Ryan Kavuma-McQueen joined Portsmouth on loan over the summer

Explosive pace, infectious energy on the field and bundles of footballing ability.

At just 17, Ryan Kavuma-McQueen has looked at home in the Championship since embarking on his first loan move away from Chelsea.

With one senior appearance to his name at Stamford Bridge, the winger swapped west London for the south coast in August and has quickly become a fan favourite at Fratton Park.

Indeed, Kavuma-McQueen was so impressive in a recent game against Sheffield United, Pompey boss John Mousinho admitted their tactic essentially became - pass him the ball as much as possible.

"For a 17-year-old to come in and play as many games as he has done is a real achievement," the Portsmouth head coach told BBC Sport.

"He's been brilliant to work with and has been absolutely unplayable in some games, for us it's now about getting him consistently to that level.

"It's very easy to forget that he's only 17 because of the way that he plays and how he carries himself - overall it's been an excellent loan so far and we're really excited to see how he goes for the rest of the season."

At international level, Kavuma-McQueen has played 31 matches for England's youth sides and scored 29 goals.

One of his most recent for England Under-18s was a stunning strike that saw him beat a number of defenders with some smart footwork before launching a right-footed rocket into the top corner from 25 yards.

For Portsmouth, he scored seven minutes into his first Championship start and has registered two assists, contributing to winning points for the Blues in games against Blackburn Rovers and Sheffield United.

"No other so-called 'big six' Premier League club has a fully homegrown 17-year-old on loan in the Championship," said BBC football news reporter Nizaar Kinsella .

"This is a source of pride within Chelsea's academy. At Championship level, only Preston's George Gryba and Wolves' Charlie Holt have made appearances at a younger age this season.

"It is clear that Kavuma-McQueen finds playing against opponents of his own age relatively straightforward.

"Securing a loan move was so important this summer, without European football, and with a large number of wide options available, opportunities were always likely to be limited at Chelsea."

So far this season, Kavuma-McQueen has featured predominantly on the left but has also played on the right wing of Portsmouth's attack.

He leads the Championship in some attacking metrics, completing the most successful take-ons (30) and attempting the joint-most dribbles (55) in the division.

He is also in the top 10 for drives into the box and carries ending in shots.

The Blues have a number of wide attackers to choose from, with Abu Kamara and Josh Murphy both proven at this level, but the teenager has displayed his credentials to play in their starting XI, making nine starts in the Championship with a further five appearances off the bench.

If he can remain fit then he will undoubtably be an important player for the rest of the 2026-27 campaign, but a sustained period of health is far from straightforward in a relentless league and a busy festive schedule to come.

Regardless of the impact that Kavuma-McQueen has over the rest of the season, there is no doubt that the experience he will gain from this loan should serve him well going forward.

Portsmouth head coach John Mousinho on Ryan Kavuma-McQueen

Mousinho has praised the winger's character after an injury setback in September after falling over advertising hoardings at Fratton Park.

He suffered a double fracture on his right hand, but opted against surgery and now wears a splint and cast for games which has delayed his full recovery to around eight weeks.

The Portsmouth boss admitted that he was probably not managing the injury in the most ideal way, but believed his decision to play on provided an insight into his mentality of wanting to make the most of the loan move.

"From a football perspective he's managing it unbelievably well and he hasn't shied away from anything on the pitch," Mousinho added.

"It's never been a concern of mine and the fact that he wanted to play and didn't want surgery tells us everything we need to know about the lad."

Pompey are enjoying a positive start to their third season back in the second tier having won promotion from League One in 2024.

They are 11th in the table and just two points outside of the newly expanded play-off positions.

Kavuma-McQueen has played plenty of minutes already - his 719 is comfortably the highest among Championship players 18 and under, but there is a slight concern Pompey could become victims of his success in terms of his immediate future.

"Arguably in the first part of Portsmouth's season, he was their best player," said BBC Radio Solent commentator Andrew Moon.

"He's fast, skillful and exciting to watch. He's also able to cope with a physical league that most teenagers can't.

"His output did drop off before the international break but there will always be some ups and downs with such a young player. Mousinho has been managing his minutes very carefully.

"He's already being watched by other clubs and Chelsea could recall him in January to send elsewhere. Portsmouth will argue strongly that Fratton Park is the best place for him to continue his development."

Ryan Kavuma-McQueen has been capped by England from under-15 to under-18 level

For his parent club, Kavuma-McQueen is seen as a talent with a genuine chance of making it at the club, despite fierce competition among the wide players already in the squad.

He joined the west London club at under-eight level and signed a scholarship in July 2025.

Prior to his move to the south coast he travelled with the senior Chelsea squad for their pre-season tour, starting against Western Sydney Wanderers down-under before his loan move.

Chelsea already have a host of highly-rated teenagers out on loan, including Jesse Derry (Sporting), Dastan Satpayev (Burnley), Reggie Walsh (Wigan Athletic), Shim Mheuka (Celtic) and Landon Emenalo (Celtic).

The club also lost Rio Ngumoha to Liverpool and Ryan McAidoo to Man City in 2024, which remains a sore point within the Surrey-based academy.

In an era of lucrative deals for players between top academies, Chelsea have not lost a player since but had to fight hard to keep Kavuma-McQueen before he signed his first professional contract in January.

By securing a move to the Championship, Kavuma-McQueen can continue his development at a high level, and his performances at Fratton Park have been noted by influential figures back in west London.

"We speak to them [Chelsea] all the time and that's a positive thing," Mousinho added.

"They would like Ryan to play as much as possible but also get the exposure of what it's like to be in and out of a first team and experience the highs and lows of football that has real consequence.

"That's been amazing in terms of Ryan's development and making sure that we keep on top of him physically and mentally.

"We have both clubs working really hard to make sure that happens and both clubs working really hard in conjunction with each other."

Perezida wa Ukraine Volodymyr Zelensky yavuze ko Vladimir Putin ari "umwicanyi", mu gusubiza Perezida w'Amerika Donald Trump wise uwo Perezida w'Uburusiya "inshuti" ye ubwo bari bari mu Bushinwa muri iki cyumweru.

Aganira n'igitangazamakuru CNN, Zelensky yavuze ko bireba Perezida w'Amerika "ukuntu yita Putin" ariko "kuri twe, ni umwanzi... kuri twe, ni umwicanyi".

Mbere y'inama ya batatu yanditse amateka yabaye ku wa kane yagiranye na Perezida w'Ubushinwa Xi Jinping na Putin, Trump yise Putin "inshuti" ye ndetse avuga ko bafitanye "umubano mwiza cyane umaze imyaka myinshi".

Ibitero by'Uburusiya byakomeje mu ijoro ryacyeye, byica abantu babiri, harimo umuhungu, naho abandi bantu 52 barakomereka mu bitero bya misile n'indege nto z'intambara zitajyamo umupilote (zizwi nka 'drones') byibasiye umujyi Zelensky avukamo wa Kryvyi Rih, uri mu karere kari rwagati mu gihugu ka Dnipropetrovsk, nkuko abategetsi babivuze.

Ikigo cya Ukraine gishinzwe ubutabazi bwihuse (DSNS) cyavuze ko abantu 11 na bo bakomerekeye mu karere ka Kharkiv kari mu majyaruguru ashyira uburasirazuba bw'igihugu, naho undi muntu umwe arakomereka i Rivne, mu majyaruguru ashyira uburengerazuba bw'icyo gihugu.

Ku wa gatanu, abantu nibura icyenda biciwe mu bitero by'Uburusiya byibasiye amateme yo mu murwa mukuru Kyiv wa Ukraine hamwe na stasiyo zitegerwamo gariyamoshi mu burengerazuba bwa Ukraine. Zelensky yavuze ko icyo gitero ari cyo "cya mbere kinini cyane kibayeho uyu mwaka", kikaba cyarakoreshejwemo misile 110, zirimo 27 zo mu bwoko bwa 'ballistic' na 'drone' zirenga 400.

Ibyo bitero byabaye hashize iminsi Ukraine yangije bikomeye iteme rya Crimea, ryo mu mwigimbakirwa wa Crimea Uburusiya bwiyometseho mu mwaka wa 2014 buwukuye kuri Ukraine.

Nyuma y'amasaha habaye ibyo bitero Uburusiya bwagabye kuri Ukraine ku wa gatanu, Trump yabwiye abanyamakuru ari mu biro bye bya White House ko Putin "yifuza cyane kurangiza intambara".

Ku wa gatanu, yagize ati: "Bombi [Zelensky na Putin] barashaka kuyirangiza kandi ni ikintu cyiza cyane ko mfitanye umubano [na bo]."

Trump yanashimangiye ko ahagaze ku byo yavuze ko Perezida w'Uburusiya ari inshuti ye ariko avuga ko atamenya niba Putin ari inshuti y'Amerika.

Ariko Zelensky yavuze ko nubwo Trump ari aho ahagaze, we abona Putin nk'"umwicanyi".

Yabwiye CNN ati: "Ntekereza ko ahanini ku bantu bo ku isi, ari umwicanyi kuko arimo kwica... arimo kwica buri munsi na buri joro."

Zelensky yanavuze ko kuvuga kuri Putin nkaho ari "inshuti" bituma "atumva igitutu gihagije".

Iyi ntambara y'amagambo ibaye mu gihe Pologne, ihana imbibi na Ukraine n'Uburusiya, yavuze ko misile y'Uburusiya yo mu bwoko bwa 'cruise' ari imwe mu bintu bitatu byavogereye ikirere cyayo mu majyepfo ashyira uburasirazuba, mu masaha ya kare yo ku wa gatanu.

Minisitiri w'ingabo wa Pologne Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz yavuze ko iyo misile yakubise mu gace k'icyaro i Nowy Lipowiec, mu ntera ya kilometero hafi 50 uvuye ku mupaka wa Ukraine.

Abategetsi bo muri Pologne bavuze ko aho hantu ari mu ntera ya kilometero hafi 100 uvuye aho ingabo z'Uburayi – zo mu bihugu 11 muri 36 bigize ihuriro ry'abakorerabushake – zari zirimo kurangiza imyitozo. Abo bategetsi bongeyeho ko indi misile na 'drone' ikoreshwa na moteri y'indege bicyekwa ko byaguye ahandi hantu habiri.

Minisitiri w'intebe wa Pologne Donald Tusk yavuze ko uko bigaragara ibyabaye bitari impanuka.

Nta muntu wakomeretse ndetse nta byatangajwe ko byangiritse ariko Pologne yavuze ko ibyabaye ari "ubushotoranyi" bw'Uburusiya.

Umunyamabanga mukuru w'umuryango wo gutabarana w'Uburayi n'Amerika (OTAN/NATO), Mark Rutte, yamaganye "ivogera rikomeye cyane ry'ikirere cya Pologne" ndetse yavuze ko OTAN yihutiye kuhageza indege z'intambara zo gutabara.

Nta cyo Uburusiya bwatangaje kuri iryo vogera, ryabaye ubwo habaga igitero kinini cyane bwagabye kuri Ukraine ku wa gatanu.

Putin yagabye igitero gisesuye kuri Ukraine kuva muri Gashyantare (2) mu mwaka wa 2022.

Karen Scarborough (left) and Anne Lindboe got to work with a two-handled saw

This year's Trafalgar Square Christmas tree has been cut down in a forest outside Oslo, ready to begin its journey to London.

The 21m (69ft) tree, nicknamed Jolly Cheery, is about 75 years old. It was felled on Friday by the Lord Mayor of Westminster, Karen Scarborough, and the Mayor of Oslo, Anne Lindboe.

Norway has sent a tree to the capital every year since 1947 as a thank you for Britain's support during World War Two, when King Haakon VII and the Norwegian government lived in exile in London.

Its lights will be switched on by the two mayors at a ceremony in the square on Thursday, 3 December.

Scarborough said: "It's my greatest honour to take part in this wonderful tradition for both the cities of Oslo and London.

"This tree is a powerful symbol of friendship and peace, reminding us to be there for one another during the festive period."

The 21m tree has been nicknamed Jolly Cheery

Scarborough thanked "the people of Oslo and Norway for this truly fabulous gift" and added: "With the care and dedication of the team, I'm sure it will look magnificent on Trafalgar Square."

Lindboe said: "Oslo has been sending a Christmas tree to London for almost eight decades, and every year we send a tree across the North Sea with the same message: we have not forgotten.

"The tradition has a powerful history, and its message remains just as relevant today.

"I hope Jolly Cheery spreads warmth and Christmas cheer to everyone who passes by, and reminds us how much it means to be there for one another, especially in difficult times."

Count the rings: Anne Lindboe (left) and Karen Scarborough (right) with a slice of the 75-year-old trunk

For the second year running, the tree was chosen with the help of a social media poll.

Organisers said it would travel by road in Norway and England using only electric and biodiesel vehicles, cutting the journey's carbon footprint by 80%. It will cross the North Sea on a regular cargo ship from the port of Brevik.

Once in London, it will be decorated in the traditional Norwegian style, with 25m strings of festoon lighting fitted with energy-efficient bulbs.

The FBI is investigating an apparent breach of its criminal information database, US media report citing two people briefed on the issue.

The National Crime Information Center (NCIC) database is used by federal and local law enforcement to share information on warrants and background checks. The BBC has contacted the FBI for comment.

This comes after string of tech outages which hit banking, air traffic control and other sectors in the US last week. Officials have said they were not caused by cyberattacks - but the blackouts have sparked scrutiny from lawmakers.

White House National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross was fired this week, with US President Donald Trump saying he was not good enough.

It would not be the first time hackers have targeted the FBI, the domestic intelligence and security service of the US.

In September, the FBI said it was investigating an apparent breach by a cyber-crime group ShinyHunters, which claimed it had stolen sensitive information on all bureau staff - around 38,000 people.

After that hack, one former FBI agent told the BBC he feared for the safety of current employees, whose personal information could soon become available online to criminals and hostile nation-state hackers.

In a separate development, NBC reported an apparent cyberattack against the US Department of Agriculture (USDA) .

Employees were informed on Thursday that its farm payment system had been targeted, NBC said.

The USDA has not publicly commented on the issue.

Rwanda’s Minister of Internal Security, Dr Vincent Biruta, has visited Egypt’s Suez Canal, one of the world’s most important maritime trade routes, as part of efforts to gain insights into its operations, strategic importance and contribution to international trade and security.

Dr Biruta was accompanied by Rwanda’s Ambassador to Egypt, Commissioner General Dan Munyuza.

The delegation was received by the Chairman of the Suez Canal Authority, Lt. Gen. Osama Rabie, who briefed them on the canal’s history, operations and role in facilitating global maritime transport.

During the visit, Biruta was taken through the canal’s operational activities and its importance in connecting maritime trade between different parts of the world.

He also visited the Suez Canal Museum, where he was briefed on the history of the waterway, its construction and subsequent expansion to accommodate larger vessels and increase its capacity.

The visit provided an opportunity for the Rwandan delegation to learn about the management of a major international maritime corridor, particularly its contribution to trade facilitation, economic development and national security.

The Suez Canal connects the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea, providing a crucial shipping route between Europe, Asia and other global markets. It is among the busiest maritime passages in the world, allowing vessels to avoid the longer journey around the southern tip of Africa.

Speaking during the visit, Dr Biruta said: “We appreciate the opportunity to learn about the history, operations and strategic importance of the Suez Canal, particularly its contribution to international trade and maritime security.”

The visit is also expected to provide insights into how strategic infrastructure can be managed to support economic interests while strengthening security and international cooperation.

For Egypt, the canal is a major economic asset and a critical source of revenue, while its strategic location makes it an important component of global supply chains and maritime security.

Javits Frimpong yishwe arashwe ubwo yari ari mu nzira arimo agenda n'amaguru ajya ku ishuri, mu karere ka the Bronx ko mu mujyi wa New York. Urupfu rwe rwateje uburakari bwinshi muri Ghana no muri Amerika, ndetse rwongera kubyutsa impaka ku rugomo rukoreshwa imbunda muri Amerika.

Umukuru w'umujyi wa New York, Zohran Mamdani, yagize ati: "Javits yari akwiriye ibyiza cyane."

Yongeyeho ati: "Nubwo yabaye i New York by'igihe gito gusa, Umujyi wa New York uzahora iteka utewe ishema no kwita Javits umwe muri twe."

Frimpong yari amaze hafi umwaka umwe ageze muri Amerika ubwo yaraswaga.

Se, Thomas Frimpong, yagize ati: "Narakoze cyane kugira ngo ngukure muri Ghana nkuzane muri Amerika kuko nashakaga ko ugira amahirwe, ejo hazaza heza kurushaho, n'amahirwe yo kugera ku kintu cyose wari ufitiye inzozi."

Nyina yahawe uruhushya ('visa') rwihutirwa rwo kuva muri Ghana akajya muri Amerika gushyinyura umuhungu we, nyuma y'igikorwa cyakozwe na Mamdani cyo kubyumvisha Perezida w'Amerika Donald Trump cyabaye mbere yaho muri uku kwezi.

Mbere, muri uku kwezi, Doris Adu Gyamfi yabwiye BBC ko ashaka "ubutabera ku muhungu wanjye", ibyo bikaba byanagarutsweho muri uwo muhango wo gushyingura wabaye ku wa gatanu.

Frimpong yarirukankanwe ubundi araraswa ku itariki ya 29 Ukwakira (10). Yajyanwe ku bitaro byo muri ako gace, ari na ho byemerejwe ko yapfuye.

Conservationists say Jersey is an "important refuge" for red squirrels

With growing concerns that red squirrels could soon become extinct in England , one Channel Island is a corner of the British Isles where they maintain a stronghold.

Jersey is home to a thriving red squirrel population, thanks to the complete absence of grey squirrels, which carry a virus deadly to their red cousins.

Red squirrels are endangered in the UK , with about 120,000 to 160,000 left in the wild and various projects are aiming to boost those numbers.

There have some strongholds in England , external , particularly islands, and 75% of the British population is in Scotland , external .

However, despite not being native to Jersey, Henry Glynn, an ecologist with the National Trust of Jersey, said they "really are iconic for Jersey".

He said: "When you speak to people who have come over to visit the island from the UK, a lot of them will say that one of the things they want to do whilst here is to see a red squirrel, because they're so rare and so difficult to see in large parts of the UK.

"That is actually really special for them."

Red squirrels are not native to Jersey, having been introduced in 1885.

However, Glynn described them as "naturalised", having become "assimilated into the natural environment" over many years.

The animals have previously featured in Visit Jersey , external tourism campaigns, including one fronted by conservationist Ben Fogle.

National Trust ecologist Henry Glynn says red squirrel sightings can be a highlight for visitors

The National Trust of Jersey said the island wa s an "important refuge" for the red squirrel, where they were " fairly widespread , external ".

It said the inland valleys and woodlands were the best places to spot them.

The species is legally protected, which means it would be a criminal offence to harm them.

Nina Powell, senior animal carer at the JSPCA [Jersey Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals], said Jersey has a "good population" of squirrels and that "you can see them almost anywhere".

While the primary reason for their success is the lack of grey squirrels, Powell said they also thrived "because people look out for them".

She said: "A lot of people do support them, put out feeders and stuff like that.

"Their habitats are decreasing everywhere... but we do have quite a lot of nature reserves.

"In some places, we've got rope bridges which really help them cross the roads, and our speed limits are quite low, so that helps them as well".

Nina Powell from the JSPCA said the red squirrels it comes into contact with can have quite different personalities

She said the JSPCA had handled 50 red squirrels so far this year, including hand-raising eight babies, called kits (kittens).

She said: "We want to keep all animals as wild as possible, so we try and be as hands-off as possible.

"Some of them don't like us... some of them are quite sweet. They really do vary in personality."

Glynn agreed that their success had come in part because of the efforts of islanders.

He said: "They're really beloved amongst the local community as well. A lot of people put out squirrel feeders or love to see them in the garden.

"We get lots of reports from people who just want to tell us they've seen them because they're so happy to have them around."

Wes Streeting told Volodymyr Zelensky he was in Kyiv to show that Europe was united in its support for Ukraine

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has justified Kyiv's repeated attacks on a critical bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea, calling it a "fair response" to 109 separate Russian attacks on bridges in Ukraine.

In comments to the BBC in Kyiv, Zelensky said the intense attacks on Ukraine by Russia that have followed the strikes on the Crimean Bridge were only a "signal that Vladimir Putin does not want to stop. He wants a reason to escalate".

He rejected the claim by the Russian president that the bridge - which links Russia to the peninsular it illegally annexed from Ukraine - was "exclusively civilian" in use.

"There are facts, not just the words of Putin. We can see," he said.

The Ukrainian president pointed to images online of tanks and other Russian military hardware using the route from Russia into occupied Crimea as a supply line and for logistics.

"If Putin used the internet, he could see that."

The Ukrainian president added that Russia had carried out attacks with missiles and drones on bridges in Ukraine.

This week's combined missile-and-drone strikes destroyed the central road section of the Crimean Bridge, collapsing part of it together with one of the two support arches into the sea and rendering the structure unusable for road traffic.

Russian attacks on Ukraine continued on Friday evening and overnight: a seven-year-old boy was killed in missile and drone strikes on Zelensky's hometown of Kryvyi Rih in the central Dnipropetrovsk region. Local officials say he had been in a playground at the time.

A 20-year-old female medic was also killed. A local official added that when rescuers rushed to the scene, the same site was targeted again with jet powered drones. Another 58 people were injured in the city.

Ukraine's state emergency service DSNS said 11 people were also injured in the north-eastern Kharkiv region, and one person in Rivne, in the north-west.

Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

Footage shows Ukrainian missile approach Crimean Bridge

Zelensky was speaking ahead of a meeting in Kyiv with UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting, who told the Ukrainian president he was here to show that Europe was united in its support.

"The more Putin tries to divide us, the more resolute we become," Streeting said.

He said that Russian missiles hitting Poland on Friday, during military exercises of the so-called Coalition of the Willing, was an "outrageous provocation".

The timing, Streeting said, seemed "more than a coincidence".

Asked by the BBC about Nato's response, he said the best way was to "do more for Ukraine" to defend itself against Putin who he called a "cold-blooded killer".

Streeting's description of Putin chimed with the comments made earlier by Zelensky, who described the Kremlin leader a "killer". This was done in response to US President Donald Trump referring this week to Putin as his "friend".

Streeting's visit to Kyiv came after European leaders meeting in Berlin on Thursday alongside US envoys said they were ready for negotiations with Moscow on ending the war in Ukraine.

"Europe has a clear and consistent and united negotiating position," UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said, while German Chancellor Friedrich Merz stressed that Moscow's "maximalist demands are not realistic".

Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner, one of the two US envoys who were in Berlin, said the US president - who had also dialled into the meeting from Air Force One - wanted to make a deal with Moscow "with Europe by his side".

Russia's Vladimir Putin has so far rejected any European role in the US-led peace talks - but earlier this week he invited European representatives to Moscow as it wanted to clarify "what Europe will bring to these talks".

That meeting in the German capital came hours after Putin had held historic trilateral talks in Shenzhen, China, with Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping.

Zelensky said he had been "sceptical" ahead of the latest round of talks, when US envoys claimed that Russia was prepared to make compromises to end the war.

"I thought [Putin] would find reason to escalate."

Speaking to the BBC, Streeting added: "Putin has absolutely no business playing the victim. He is the aggressor in this war. He provoked an illegal invasion of Ukraine. And all of us, right throughout the world, need to judge Putin not on his words, but on his actions."

In a separate development on Saturday, Finland said it "detected a drone strike on a Russian merchant vessel" in the eastern Gulf of Finland, "in an international maritime area".

The Finnish defence ministry said in a statement that the vessel was damaged, without giving any further details.

It added that "temporary restrictions on aviation and maritime areas in the eastern Gulf of Finland" were now reinstated for safety reasons.

Russia has not publicly commented on the issue.

KIGALI – When Ogbonna Kingsley aka Doctall first visited Rwanda, he had no idea that a neighborhood in Kigali would eventually give him a new identity, or that country thousands of kilometers from his Nigerian home would become somewhere he increasingly describes as his own.

His first name for the Rwandan identity he was creating was Kachikuru, inspired by Kicukiro, where he was staying during his visit. He had enjoyed the neighborhood so much that he decided to turn its name into part of his comedy persona.

But Rwandans who encountered the name were not entirely impressed, telling him it sounded more like a cooking stove than a human being.

He eventually settled on Ntakirutimana, a Kinyarwanda name he explains as meaning that nobody is like God. The name stuck, and so did his affection for the country that inspired it.

Today, the Nigerian comedian, popularly known as Ntakirutimana, has built an unusual relationship with Rwanda, regularly entertaining audiences with videos in which he embraces Rwandan culture, jokes about everyday life and introduces himself as the son of President Paul Kagame.

The latter is a playful identity he has taken particularly seriously in his own humorous way. He says his admiration for the President was actually what introduced him to Rwanda.

“I fell in love with the President. In fact, I got to know Rwanda through the President, who is my father,” he said during an interview on Kigali Today’s Beyond the Scroll podcast.

Ogbonna speaks about Rwanda with the enthusiasm of someone who believes he has discovered something he wants to be part of. Having travelled to different African countries, he says the experience has shaped his appreciation of the opportunities and everyday conditions he associates with Rwanda.

He particularly admires what he considers the country’s relative stability and the leadership behind it, often contrasting his experiences with those in Nigeria, where unreliable electricity and the cost of accessing basic services remain familiar frustrations.

“Sometimes you don’t even know what you have until you visit other African countries. I believe Rwandans should appreciate what they have rather than take it for granted,” he told his Rwandan hosts.

His admiration for Kagame is equally personal in the way he describes it. Asked what he would do if granted five minutes with the President, Kingsley said he had never met him and would probably spend most of the encounter overwhelmed by emotion.

“I might just use the first four minutes to cry. And then probably use the remaining one minute to appreciate him, thank him very much for what he’s doing for Rwanda and Africa,” he said.

Behind the colorful personality is a man who describes himself as an introvert, preferring the quiet of his home to the constant activity that comes with public life.

He says his ideal day involves little more than sleeping, waking up and eating, a contrast to the energetic character his audiences encounter online. Yet comedy has taken him across audiences and borders.

He recalls that his career reached an important turning point in 2021 when he secured his first endorsement deal in Nigeria, an opportunity that showed him the financial possibilities of turning entertainment into a profession.

Like other content creators, he has experienced periods when demanding schedules and the uncertainties of the industry made him question whether he had chosen the right career. But messages from people who say his videos have helped them through difficult moments have given him reasons not to give up.

“People tell me, ‘Ntakirutimana, I watched your video, I was depressed and now I’m happy.’ Those are the kind of words that give me hope and encourage me to keep doing what I’m doing,” he said.

It is a responsibility he appears to take seriously, particularly as he describes himself as a Pan-African who wants to use entertainment to promote the continent rather than simply build an individual following.

His growing connection with Rwanda has also made him consider a more permanent presence in the country. During the interview, he confirmed that he was working towards relocating, although he was reluctant to discuss the details.

For Ogbonna , one way of turning that attachment into something lasting is through the Nakirutimana Experience, a comedy show he says he intends to organize annually to connect with his Rwandan audience.

The event brings together his Nigerian identity and the Rwandan audience he has cultivated, with local comedians also joining him on stage. He hopes future editions will grow to include international performers, potentially bringing entertainers from the United States and elsewhere to Rwanda.

He is also keen to encourage young Africans interested in content creation, drawing from his own experience of building a career in an industry where visibility does not always translate into immediate success.

His advice is to stop waiting for perfect conditions before taking the first step. “You have to start from where you are. Just start and be consistent. That discipline and authenticity matter as much as talent,” he said.

For someone who has turned a neighborhood name into an identity recognized by Rwandan audiences, the idea of starting where you are seems to have acquired a particular meaning.

Ogbonna is still Nigerian, but through comedy, cultural exchange and an affection he makes little effort to conceal, he has found a second home in Rwanda. He appears content building that connection one joke, one performance and one Kinyarwanda word at a time.

He has been in Rwanda since Monday, November 16, 2026. He is set to entertain Rwandans at a “Thank God” It’s Funny comedy show scheduled for November 27, 2026.

KIGALI – Oceane Kamikazi remembers how difficult it was to achieve a typing speed of 50 words per minute during her first trimester at Kepler College.

Although facilitators had set the target as something students could reach within that period, repeated attempts left her falling short, with scores of 44, 42 and 45 words per minute.

By the second-to-last session, she was beginning to lose hope and had considered trying again the following term. When she decided to make one final attempt, this time she reached the target.

“I didn’t just gain a typing speed that day. I gained staying power,” said Kamikazi, who graduated with a Bachelor of Arts in Project Management.

Speaking on behalf of the Class of 2026, she recalled the deadlines, presentations and demanding group assignments that had tested students throughout their three-year journey.

Those experiences, she said, had also taught them to depend on one another, with classmates offering help when others struggled to keep up.

Her message to fellow graduates was that the determination they had developed at college should now be put to use beyond the classroom. “Kepler College did not train us to wait for solutions; it built us to create them. We should use these skills to address challenges in our communities and across Africa,” Kamikazi said.

The graduation marked Kepler College’s second graduating class and the 11th cohort of students graduating through its partnership with Southern New Hampshire University (SNHU).

In his remarks, Kepler College Vice Chancellor Prof. Baylie Damtie Yeshita said the institution measures the value of its education by their ability to translate knowledge into practical skills and secure meaningful employment.

He said 90 per cent of Kepler graduates consistently secure employment in their fields within six months of graduation, while 49 per cent of the Class of 2026 had already secured employment before completing their studies.

“The outcome that matters most to our goal is not a certificate on the wall. It is a dignified work and a dignified life,” Yeshita said.

Careers, Change and The Value of Persistence

Presiding over the graduation as guest of honor, Sports Minister Nelly Mukazayire urged graduates to prepare for careers that may take unexpected turns, drawing from her own experience of moving through different professional roles before becoming Minister of Sports.

Although she had not studied engineering, her first job was as an administrative assistant in a construction company. Her career later took her through other responsibilities, showing that professional life does not always follow the path people initially imagine.

“The feeling of not knowing what you are doing is not a sign that you are behind. It is a tax you pay to move forward. I encourage you to remain curious, embrace change and find the courage to begin again when necessary,” she cautioned.

Mukazayire also asked them to value the people who had supported them along the way, including family members, friends and classmates. She reminded them that their achievements were not reached alone and urged them to carry gratitude and kindness into their working lives.

Kepler Chief Executive Officer Nathalie Munyampenda reinforced the importance of patience, cautioning graduates against measuring their progress against the lives they see on social media.

She compared personal development to building a house, explaining that every completed structure takes time and a series of steps. Graduates, she said, should allow themselves the same room to grow rather than rushing to match other people’s achievements.

“What is important in life is to run at your own pace. Success requires people to understand and respect their own process,” she said.

Munyampenda pointed to the changes brought by artificial intelligence, saying that graduates would need to keep developing their ability to think and put ideas into action. “The only thing that remains after AI is thinking and doing,” she said.

The different messages returned to a shared expectation that the value of the education graduates received would ultimately be seen in what they do with it.

That call to contribute beyond personal achievement was also central to the message delivered by Rodwell Mangisi, Director of Digital Economy at the Mastercard Foundation, who challenged graduates to see their education as a responsibility to society.

“Your education is not only a private achievement. It is a public responsibility,” he told the graduates, encouraging them to create businesses, lead teams, solve problems and open opportunities for others.

Mangisi drew on his own experience growing up in Rimuka, a small town in Kadoma, Zimbabwe, where he sold ice pops and popcorn at a bus terminal at the age of 10.

At the time, he was simply trying to earn money, but the activity introduced him to lessons in business, including finding suppliers, estimating demand, managing stock and organizing his time around school.

He later moved to South Africa for further studies, where financial difficulties made it hard to pay his fees. A parent of a student he tutored eventually offered to cover the costs, giving him the chance to concentrate on his education.

When Mangisi later tried to repay the benefactor, the man declined and told him: “I did not help you so that you could come and repay me back. I helped you so that you could go out there and help someone else.”

The instruction to “pay it forward” became one of the principles he carried into his career. He urged graduates to remember those who had supported them and, in turn, help others access opportunities.

He also cautioned them against treating their degrees as the final measure of their abilities. His own career moved from electrical engineering into electronics, software development, data and analytics, and eventually digital solutions and commercial leadership.

“Your degree is the foundation. It is not the destination,” he said, advising graduates to remain open to learning and to treat failure as information that can help them improve rather than a judgement of their abilities.

The ceremony brought together 322 students from eight African countries, comprising 171 graduates from Southern New Hampshire University (SNHU) and 141 from Kepler College.

Others are 10 Arizona State University master’s graduands from the Kepler College Plus Program, whose degrees in Business Analytics and Global Technology and Development will be formally conferred in December 2026.

Women accounted for 56.8 per cent of the graduating class, while 28.3 per cent were from refugee backgrounds. Several graduates also received special recognition.

Irirenga Gaju Ingrid, Ruzibiza Umukundwa Linda and Yaravuze Syverson received Determination Awards, while Lygie Princess Irakoze was given the Resilience Award.

Auguste Dufitimana and Alexis Niyomugabo were recognized for their support to fellow students in the SNHU program and the 2026 Project Management cohort, respectively.

Inama y'Igihugu y'Abagore (CNF) irasaba abagabo guha urubuga abagore babo, bakabashyigikira, bakanabagaragariza ko babafitiye icyizere.

Ni bumwe mu butumwa bwatanzwe n'ubuyobozi bwa CNF, kuri uyu wa Gatandatu, ubwo mu bice bitandukanye by'Igihugu haberaga amatora y'abajyanama rusange mu Nama Njyanama z'Uturere.

Mu kiganiro kidasanzwe cyanyuze kuri KT Radio, Umunyamabanga Nshingwabikorwa wa CNF, Marie Médiatrice Umubyeyi, yagaragaje ko hari abagore biyumvamo ubushobozi ariko bakabuzwa n'abagabo babo.

Yagize ati "Twarabibonye, hari umugore umwe warimo wandika avuga ati mu Mudugudu wanjye batoye umuntu nabo babona ko bidakwiye, banyamamaje ariko umugabo yaranyangiye kandi ntabwo najya kubaka umudugudu mu rugo iwanjye bitameze neza. Urumva ko umugore yiyumvagamo ko yabikora kandi yabishobora."

Yungamo ati "Ariko kubera ko uwo babana atabyumva kandi mbere na mbere habaho ubwo bwumvikane, iyo bigeze mu gufata icyo cyemezo uwo babana yamweretse ko bidashoboka. Ibyo nabyo ni izindi mpungenge zibaho, bikaba atari mu by'ukuri gutinya politike nkuko bivugwa, ahubwo abo babana nabo bakaba batamushyigikira."

Ahanini ngo abagabo babiterwa no kumva ko igihe abagore baramuka bagiye mu miyoborere y'inzego z'ibanze, mu rugo bazamubura ku buryo hari byinshi bishobora kutitabwaho bikagira ingaruka ku burere bw'abana.

Ibi ariko si ko Umubyeyi abibona kuko asanga ari urwitwazo.

Ati "Aho abantu bafatanyije n'ubundi uburere bw'abana bureba umugore n’umugabo. None se iyo umwe ari mu kazi ko uyu munsi twisanga tudakorera hamwe, uhari ntabijyamo? Wenda ntiyabikora nk'ubimenyereye ariko agira ibyo akora kandi ubuzima bugakomeza. Abagore dukunda kuvuga ngo baritinya ariko baba batinya ibyo byose."

Uwitwa Marenga wo mu Karere ka Gisagara, yasabye ko iki kibazo cyafatirwa ingamba kugira ngo abagabo bashobora ku byumva no kubyakira neza nkuko bigenda ku bagore igihe bumvise ko abagabo babo bagiriwe icyizere bagatorerwa umwanya runaka.

Yagize ati "Ko nshimye ko icyo kibazo kibaho nkuko mwabivuze, murimo guteganya iki kugira ngo niba ntabyemeye umugore wanjye ntagomba kwiyamamaza, kandi we aramutse abyanze jye ubwanjye Marenga ngomba kwiyamamaza. Iryo pfundo muzarifungura mute kugira ngo twese duhurize ku mujo umwe kugira ngo tuyobore igihugu cyacu."

Igisubizo Marenga yahawe ni uko nta cyakorwa hatabayeho ubwumvikane, ariko anabwirwa ko burya kubibuza umugore ari kimwe mu ihohotera aba akorewe kuko aba abujijwe ibyo afitiye uburenganzira.

Umubyeyi ati "Kuki utareka umuntu ngo agende urebe na bya bindi wavugaga ko atazabasha kubihuza, urebe ko atabihuze. Ahubwo se kuki utakumva ko ubushobozi usanzwe umubonamo bwo gukora bya bindi umutegerejeho mu rugo, ashobora no kubikora mu Mudugudu wanyu mukamererwa neza kurushaho."

Amatora yabaye kuri uyu wa Gatandatu ni icyiciro gikomeye mu gushyiraho inzego z'ubuyobozi zegerejwe abaturage, kuko abatorwa bazagira uruhare mu gufata ibyemezo bijyanye n'imiyoborere, igenamigambi n'iterambere ry'Uturere.

Agamije kandi kuzuza imyanya umunani y'Abajyanama rusange muri buri Nama Njyanama y'Akarere.

Buri Nama Njyanama y'Akarere igimba kuba igizwe n'abantu 17, barimo Abajyanama rusange 8, Abajyanama b'abagore 5, bangana nibura na 30%.

Abandi bahagarariye ibyiciro byihariye bine, birimo abagore, urubyiruko, abafite ubumuga n'abikorera.

Abajyanama batanu b'abagore bo batowe ku wa 17 Ugushyingo 2026, mu gihe amatora y'abajyanama rusange ari yo yabaye kuri uyu wa 21 Ugushyingo.

Angela Constance announced the review after a whistleblower leaked a document containing details about avoidable deaths

The Scottish government has ordered a review into hepatobiliary surgery at NHS Grampian after a whistleblower leaked a document showing 19 avoidable deaths at the health board.

Dr Mohammed Habib claimed he had contacted the Scottish government on four separate occasions and had gone to the police and the lord advocate with his concerns about patient safety at the board.

In a report from 2022, which was only released by Habib on Thursday, it was found 19 of the 31 deaths in liver and pancreatic surgery cases were avoidable.

The surgeon also said two people had died after having the wrong procedure performed on them and has called for the health board to face a corporate homicide inquiry.

Health Secretary Angela Constance has now announced an independent review to look at how concerns raised about liver, gallbladder and bile duct surgery, including those by Habib, were handled by the board and the Scottish government.

It will identify weaknesses in governance, missed opportunities, unreasonable delay, and gaps in accountability.

Constance said Habib's concerns were "deeply concerning and of the utmost seriousness".

Dr Mohammed Habib has called for the health board to face a corporate homicide inquiry

"Following discussion with the first minister, I am today commissioning an urgent and fully independent review of how concerns about hepatobiliary (HPB) surgery in NHS Grampian was handled, including the 2022 report into the deaths of patients who underwent HPB surgery," she said.

"Patient safety and high-quality care must always be the first concern of all those who work in, and with, the NHS."

She said that if any patients had questions or needed advice and support they should contact the NHS Grampian helpline on 08085 202030.

Constance added: "My thoughts are with anyone who has lost a loved one and I am acutely aware of the courage it has taken Dr Habib to come forward.

"I recognise he has sought to do this repeatedly, over a number of years, to both to the Scottish government and several other bodies.

"Patients and staff in Grampian have the right to expect full transparency and independent assurance that when valid concerns are raised, they are properly and robustly pursued. That is what this review will seek to establish."

Constance will make a statement in Holyrood on Tuesday, where she is expected to lay out the timetable and announce who will lead the review.

The Scottish government has said action will be taken quickly when required as part of the process to refer any issues – including potential criminality – to the relevant authorities without waiting for the final report.

The announcement comes after First Minister John Swinney announced a review of how the government handles correspondence, after he claimed he first heard of three letters sent to him by Habib on Thursday.

Humza Yousaf was health secretary at the time of Dr Habib's report.

He told BBC Scotland News he supported "further dramatic action" being taken in relation to NHS Grampian.

A spokesperson for Yousaf - who went on to become first minister before resigning in May 2024 – said: "Humza supports full transparency about what happened at NHS Grampian and will co-operate fully with any review that takes place.

"He has made it clear that he supports minutes from the period in question being released.

"As health secretary, Humza met whistleblowing champions in health boards across Scotland, and he remains clear that staff who raise patient safety concerns must be listened to and protected.

"It takes real courage to do what Dr Habib has done, and he should be commended for refusing to let these concerns go."

On Tuesday, Constance appointed an expert health team to oversee NHS Grampian improvements.

She said the "external intervention support team", comprising experienced senior NHS leaders, would work alongside Grampian's health team to provide "intensive turnaround support".

Healthcare Improvement Scotland has also been asked to complete an early review of NHS Grampian within three months to assess progress, followed by ongoing reviews, to provide independent assurance.

Ubu butumwa bwatanzwe na Marie Médiatrice Umubyeyi, Umunyamabanga Nshingwabikorwa w’Inama y’Igihugu y’Abagore, mu kiganiro cyatambutse kuri KT Radio kuri uyu wa Gatandatu, tariki ya 21 Ugushyingo 2026, ubwo mu gihugu habaga amatora y’abajyanama rusange mu Nama Njyanama z’Uturere.

Umubyeyi yavuze ko kuri iyi nshuro amatora ari kubera mu turere 27, kuko uturere dutatu tugize Umujyi wa Kigali tutarimo, bitewe n’imiterere yihariye y’imiyoborere y’Umujyi wa Kigali.

Yagarutse ku bagore bagifite impungenge zo kwinjira muri politiki, bamwe bakabitinya bitewe n’amateka u Rwanda rwanyuzemo. Yavuze ko muri iki gihe igihugu gifite ubuyobozi bwiza bwahaye amahirwe buri wese, ku buryo n’abagore bakwiye kwitinyuka bakagira uruhare mu miyoborere.

Ati: “Uruhare rw’umugore mu miyoborere ni ngombwa, kuko na kera bavugaga ko nta Mwami wategekaga adafite umugabekazi ndetse n’umwamikazi. Ibyo byose byerekana uruhare rw’umugore mu miyoborere myiza.”

Umubyeyi yavuze ko mbere y’aya matora bafashije abagore guhindura imyumvire, cyane cyane abumvaga ko badakwiye kujya muri politiki. Banabahuguye kugira ngo barusheho kwigirira icyizere, kwitinyuka no kumenya kuvugira mu ruhame.

Ati: “Politiki si mbi iyo ikozwe neza. Ubuyobozi dufite ubu si nk’ubwa Leta yabanjirije iyi, kuko yo yapyinagazaga umugore, ugasanga nta gaciro bamuha. Ariko Leta yacu yahaye umugore ijambo, kuko yamuhaye inzira zose zimwinjiza muri politiki.”

Yashishikarije abagore bahataniye imyanya mu Nama Njyanama z’Uturere kwiyumvamo ubushobozi, bakamenya ko bashyigikiwe n’ubuyobozi bwabahaye amahirwe yo kwinjira muri izo nshingano, kugira ngo batange umusanzu wabo mu kubaka igihugu.

Abagore bari mu bahatanira imyanya mu Nama Njyanama z’Uturere

Mu rwego rwo kurushaho kugaragaza uruhare rw’abagore muri aya matora, KT Radio yimuriye ibyicaro byayo mu Ntara y’Amajyepfo, ikorera mu turere twa Muhanga, Huye na Gisagara, aho yagarutse no ku bagore bahataniye kwinjira mu Nama Njyanama z’utwo turere.

Umunyamakuru Ephrem Murindabigwi yavuze ko mu bagore biyamamazaga muri utwo turere harimo benshi bafite amashuri ahagije, aho bamwe bageze ku rwego rw’ikiciro cya gatatu cya Kaminuza, ndetse bakaba bagaragaza ubushobozi n’icyizere bafite cyo kujya mu buyobozi bw’inzego z’ibanze no gutanga umusanzu wabo mu iterambere ry’igihugu.

Yagaragaje kandi ko abagore benshi bari mu bakandida biyamamaza basanzwe bafite izindi nshingano, zirimo izo mu bucuruzi no mu zindi nzego z’ubuyobozi.

Yavuze ko iyo bumvise imigabo n’imigambi yabo, bagaragaza ubushobozi n’ubushake bwo kujya mu buyobozi, bikaba bitanga icyizere ko bashobora kuzuza neza inshingano igihe baba batowe.

Amatora y’abagize Inama Njyanama z’Uturere ateye ate?

Amatora y’inzego z’ibanze mu Rwanda akorwa mu byiciro bitandukanye, kuva ku rwego rw’Umudugudu kugera ku Karere, hakurikijwe gahunda ya Komisiyo y’Igihugu y’Amatora.

Mu matora y’uyu munsi, tariki ya 21 Ugushyingo 2026, haratorwa abajyanama rusange umunani muri buri Nama Njyanama y’Akarere. Aya matora akorwa mu buryo buziguye, aho inteko itora igizwe n’abahagarariye inzego zitandukanye ku rwego rw’Akarere ari bo batora.

Ku wa 24 Ugushyingo hazatorwa Biro y’Inama Njyanama n’abagize Komite Nyobozi y’Akarere, barimo Umuyobozi w’Akarere n’abamwungirije babiri.

Aya matora ni kimwe mu byiciro bigamije kuvugurura inzego z’imiyoborere zegerejwe abaturage mu byiciro bitandukanye by’Abanyarwanda mu gufata ibyemezo.

Fausto Isidro "Chapo Isidro" Meza Flores was detained by Mexican special forces on Friday

A Mexican drug lord who was on the FBI's 10 most wanted list has been arrested following a shoot-out with Mexican authorities.

Fausto Isidro "Chapo Isidro" Meza Flores was detained along with his lieutenant by Mexican special forces in Guasave, Sinaloa on Friday, Mexico's defence secretariat said.

Meza Flores was wanted in Mexico on organised crime charges, while he has been accused of "flooding the US with fentanyl, cocaine, heroin and other deadly drugs" by the FBI. The US is seeking his extradition.

Mexico has stepped up efforts to tackle drug-related crime after coming under pressure from US President Donald Trump since he returned to the White House.

Meza Flores, the leader of the Meza Flores Organisation, also known as the Guasave Cartel, is thought to have been active in the drug trafficking trade since the 1990s but managed to evade authorities till now by maintaining a relatively low profile.

Using US intelligence on his whereabouts, Mexican special forces descended on his location using "stealth and surprise", establishing a perimeter to prevent him from escaping and reinforcements arriving, Mexico's defence secretariat said.

However, they "came under attack from gunfire and explosives" before entering the property and arresting Meza Flores and his second-in-command, it added.

Videos circulating online appear to show helicopters firing streams of bullets towards the ground in Guasave. Others appear to show people at a baseball stadium fleeing as they hear shooting sounds.

A number of vehicles were pictured burning on a highway near Los Mochis, Sinaloa, after Fausto Isidro "Chapo Idisro" Meza Flores was arrested

The two detainees were subsequently flown to Mexico City to face prosecution, the defence secretariat said.

When he was added to the FBI's most-wanted list in 2025, he was accused of "heinous crimes" including kidnapping, extortion and torture.

Then-acting FBI director Brian Driscoll said Meza Flores and his organisation had also unleashed a "scourge of illicit drugs" into the US via its southern border with Mexico.

He was initially charged with drug trafficking in the US in 2012 before being charged again in 2019.

The 44-year-old is alleged to have conspired to manufacture and distribute large quantities of cocaine, heroin, methamphetamine and marijuana between 2005 and 2019.

Meza Flores was originally a high-ranking member of the Beltrán Leyva Organization, but a split between rival factions led to a surge of violence and prompted him to establish his own cartel by 2013.

His organisation has also engaged in what US officials described as an "extremely violent turf war" with the Sinaloa Cartel, one of the most powerful drug trafficking gangs, which operates in the same region.

Meza Flores was added to the FBI's most-wanted list after Mexican authorities reportedly linked his cartel to 20 million fentanyl pills they seized in 2024.

Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum has taken a tougher stance on the country's cartels in a bid to resist US intervention on Mexican soil. Mexico has welcomed closer collaboration but resisted US boots on the ground.

Trump made stemming the flow of drugs into the US across its southern border one of his key election pledges.

MN202611_1gwqmeyijtk.t:
Elliot Anderson and Ayyoub Bouaddi both joined Manchester City in the summer

There may have been some eyebrows raised before kick-off when Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca decided to drop club record signing Enzo Fernandez to the bench against Fulham .

Fernandez's lengthy excursions back home to Argentina for their two fixtures during the international break may have been a factor in Maresca's thinking when selecting his starting XI for this game.

If it was, the Italian refrained from giving that as a reason. "I just think for this game it's better having Ayyoub Bouaddi in there," he told TNT Sports shortly before kick-off.

Even so, the move was a significant one as his side were in desperate need of victory after suffering three straight Premier League defeats. That winless streak extended to four after being held to a 1-1 draw.

Maresca had an opportunity to fix the issues in his set-up during the two-week break and admitted on Friday he was searching for "more balance" in the "defensive line, midfield and up front".

The pairing of the steady Bouaddi and all-action Elliot Anderson in the centre of the park was the crucial call, and it may have given Maresca some idea as to how to approach the forthcoming run of games.

"Ayyoub with Elliot were both really good," said Maresca. "Today we used Elliot a bit more attacking midfielder, he arrived inside the box and scored a fantastic goal, he had three or four moments around the box where he was really dangerous.

"It is another solution for us. In this moment, we are trying to know each other more as players and also to find the right solution."

Anderson rescues Man City point against Fulham

Anderson steps up, Berge impresses - player ratings for Man City v Fulham

Loud jeers greeted the full-time whistle at Etihad Stadium, a culmination of the feeling that was brewing from the home supporters throughout the game.

There was a nervous tension from the beginning, which seemed to seep on to the players on the pitch.

City displayed a flat first-half performance in which they fell behind courtesy of Rodrigo Muniz's superb curling effort, and they needed a stunning second-half volley from Anderson to rescue a point.

The England international is restricted to sitting in front of the back four when Fernandez is in the side, but has the licence to roam when Bouaddi is deployed beside him.

Aside from scoring a spectacular first Premier League goal for City, Anderson created a match-high three chances and had a 100% success rate from 16 passes in the final third of the pitch.

He also had more touches in the opposition box (7), contested more duels than any other player (17) and no-one else managed to win possession back more times than him.

After dragging his side level, another marauding run into the box was snuffed out by the visiting defenders before Rayan Cherki was brought on, which meant Anderson had to retreat back down the pitch.

Maresca needed to change things in order to apply some fresh impetus in the attacking third, but the substitution of Cherki for Phil Foden seemed to limit Anderson's capabilities.

"It's not a good result, especially off the back of three losses," former City goalkeeper Joe Hart told BBC Sport. "There was some good stuff in there.

"It felt like Elliot Anderson was going to take the game by the scruff of the neck but then Cherki came on and took his position. So he [Anderson] didn't have as much of an impact on the game.

"I understood the change - when the lines are deep, there were chances of Cherki unlocking Fulham , but they just defended so well and they also offered a threat on the break."

City hauled their midfield to the tune of £327m with the signings of trio Fernandez, Anderson and Bouaddi.

The £125m club record acquisition Fernandez had made the 14,000-mile round-trip from Manchester to Buenos Aires for Argentina's friendlies against Uruguay and Costa Rica.

The trip allowed him to take the opportunity to pay a visit to boyhood club River Plate, but it is at his current club where there are question marks as to how he fits into the side.

Bouaddi's presence provides more insurance in front of the defence and the 19-year-old Moroccan has the ability to keep the ball ticking.

It means Anderson can play his natural game - but where, then, does Fernandez fit in?

The number 10 position tends to be occupied by either Cherki or Foden, while Maresca pointed out in his pre-match news conference that City "won games with Enzo and lost games with Enzo".

But the manager clearly has to work out how to get the best out of Fernandez, who was given the final five minutes against Fulham in place of Bouaddi.

"There is no point in having a brilliant squad like Manchester City if you are not going to take that into account," said Hart.

"It's very much understandable, if you're going to have a squad and you trust everyone - if someone's done the travelling, he has done the game time, you have got to expect to not use him as much."

City host Napoli in the Champions League on Tuesday followed by a huge trip to Arsenal next Sunday, knowing they could head to the Emirates eight points behind the champions.

Maresca added: "For sure we don't like these kind of moments in terms of four games in a row without a win

"We also know that, unfortunately, it is normal or part of the path, you go through these kind of moments. It is important that we find a way to keep clean sheets that sometimes you need to win games 1-0 for a small difference."

Mikel Arteta's men know all about that and City now need to take a leaf out of their book.

MN202611_6r6nm9zk33.t:
Pugh said the Strait of Hormuz has an "extraordinary natural world" beneath the surface

A British endurance swimmer has completed a three-day swim through the Strait of Hormuz to draw attention to what he says is the environmental cost of the conflict involving Iran.

Lewis Pugh, who is a UN Patron of the Oceans, swam about 15km (9.3 miles) through the strategic waterway, a key route for oil shipments from the Middle East.

Pugh, 56, who was born in Plymouth, Devon said "war causes immense human suffering" but nature is "another casualty that receives far too little attention".

He is calling for an end to the fighting, the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and action to address environmental damage caused by the conflict.

The Strait of Hormuz carries a significant share of global oil shipments from the Middle East

The swimmer is believed to be the first person to attempt a long-distance swim in the Strait of Hormuz since the conflict began in March .

He swam from Musandam Island in the strait to the Cape of Hormuz, at the northern tip of Oman's Musandam Peninsula.

According to the Lewis Pugh Foundation, an oil tanker was struck by a projectile about 4km (2.5 miles) from where he was swimming on the first day.

On the second day, he saw flames rising above a headland separating him from the burning liquefied petroleum gas carrier Tara Gas and later passed close to the vessel while it was still on fire.

"My immediate thoughts were for the seafarers on board," Pugh said.

"The flames were enormous. These vessels carry highly flammable gases, and an attack on one can have catastrophic consequences - not just for crew members, but also on the surrounding marine environment."

Pugh has completed long-distance swims in every ocean of the world

Pugh said environmental damage caused by conflict often receives less attention than the human cost.

"War causes immense human suffering. Lives are lost, families are torn apart, and homes, hospitals and schools can be destroyed in minutes," he said.

"But there is another casualty that receives far too little attention: nature itself. And the damage can last long after the fighting has stopped."

The Strait of Hormuz is one of the world's most important shipping routes and is also home to wildlife including dugongs, sea turtles and whale sharks.

Pugh said oil spills and other contamination could have long-term consequences for marine ecosystems including coral reefs, seagrass meadows and mangrove forests.

MN202611_1q4pxs6hv6s.t:
Xabi Alonso was appointed Chelsea manager on a four-year deal in May

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso is already in firefighting mode.

His team were booed by their own supporters at several points during a dominant 4-1 Leeds victory at Stamford Bridge, their first win there since 1999.

The first negative reaction came at half-time while the score was still 1-1. The ground then began to empty after the third and fourth Leeds goals, and the fans remaining voiced their dissent once more at the final whistle.

Although there were mitigating circumstances, including a potentially harsh penalty decision against them and the loss of midfielder Moises Caicedo to injury, joining a five-strong list of players on the treatment table, the defeat was thoroughly deserved.

It leaves Chelsea with three losses in their past four Premier League matches and they have slipped from fifth place to eighth, already 14 points behind league leaders Arsenal .

In October, Tottenham won at Stamford Bridge for only the second time in the Premier League era, while the 1-0 defeat at bottom club Sunderland before the international break was another alarm bell.

It is the first time since 1967 that Chelsea have lost at home to both Leeds and Spurs in the same season.

"We need to find solutions, for sure, because there will be setbacks during any game," Alonso said after the match.

"To be able to go through that and to know that it's still so long to play, it's something mandatory in this competition and today I felt that probably we are in a fragile moment mentally.

"When we received a punch we didn't recover that strongly."

Okafor double delivers rare win for Leeds at Chelsea

'Officials can't use common sense' - was Rogers handball correct?

Indeed, even when Chelsea have been winning matches, they have often looked unconvincing.

Yet Blues supporters chanted their new manager's name and seemed optimistic after the summer transfer business - despite a disappointing 10th-place finish last season.

Club record £117m signing Morgan Rogers was joined by the experienced trio of Emiliano Martinez, Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson.

It was the clinical finishing of Rogers, along with Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro earlier in the season, that masked the underlying fragility of Alonso's team.

Before this weekend, the Blues ranked 14th for expected goal difference and were joint 12th in Opta's expected points table.

After their latest setback, ex-England forward and BBC Match of the Day pundit Alan Shearer said: " Chelsea were all over the place. Once Moises Caicedo went off injured early on, there was no physicality and they looked weak.

"They hardly created anything going forward and the back four didn't look comfortable. There was no desire, cohesion or fight from the home side, but we shouldn't take anything away from Leeds .

"Two weeks ago Chelsea were bullied by Sunderland centre-forward Brian Brobbey and they let Dominic Calvert-Lewin do the same today, which is alarming.

"It's fair to say Xabi Alonso's honeymoon period is over. He needs to tell his players this simply isn't good enough. They are miles off it and have to do better in every department."

Xabi Alonso post-match interview - Chelsea v Leeds United

In Alonso's defence, Chelsea had problems before his arrival.

They finished 10th last season, having been outrun in 37 of their 38 matches, and had three managers during a chaotic campaign.

Remarkably, Chelsea have seven more points from corresponding fixtures this season and last, but it mostly serves to show how low the bar was set.

Champions League qualification was again the club's pre-season target and Alonso's appointment was designed to bring stability and authority.

The former Real Madrid and Liverpool midfielder had an impressive playing career and earned much early admiration as a manager, guiding Bayer Leverkusen to a league and cup double in 2024.

However, the Spaniard, who was sacked by Real Madrid last season, has yet to establish any real consistency - beyond his defence leaking goals regularly.

Only Crystal Palace , Coventry City and Ipswich Town have conceded more goals than Chelsea this season.

Chelsea are also now averaging fewer than a goal per game since Joao Pedro suffered a thigh injury in training. Alongside Pedro and now Caicedo, Jorrel Hato, Maxence Lacroix, Reece James and Jamie Gittens are also injured.

It highlights how they have gained little benefit of having a season without European football.

Alonso is also beginning to face criticism from sections of the fanbase for both his team selections and substitutions.

Chief among the reasons is the constant chopping and changing of the starting XI, having now made 28 line-up changes (behind only Tottenham ) while also switching between back-four and back-three systems.

In addition, Alonso is being criticised for his use of personnel, having deployed Pedro Neto as a striker on two occasions and, some would argue, not made enough use of exciting young winger Estevao.

Against Leeds he gave striker Emmanuel Emegha his first start alongside Estevao and, although the Dutch striker scored, the pair were the first players he substituted while Chelsea were chasing the game at 3-1 down.

Similarly, his late in-game interventions are under scrutiny, including the decision to bring on striker Welbeck only in the 90th minute of the defeat by Spurs .

He took until the 64th minute to make changes against Leeds when Chelsea were already 3-1 down. Only three clubs had made more substitutions in the last 15 minutes than Chelsea in the league this season.

Given Leeds ' strengths, Chelsea should have been better prepared for what was coming. Before kick-off, Leeds had applied more high-intensity pressures in the opposition half than any other team in the Premier League.

They had also generated the most expected goals from set-pieces and won the most duels. Leeds maintained those trends at Stamford Bridge against a Chelsea side often accused of being soft.

Chelsea have had problems in recent seasons, but this was still their worst home defeat since a 4-1 loss to Brentford in 2022.

Likewise, it is almost uncharted territory in Alonso's managerial career, having only previously lost at home by a three-goal margin once.

The stadium emptied and supporters again left early.

Players displayed negative body language and argued with one another both during the match and after the final whistle.

As a result, Alonso has gone from needing to fix defensive issues to dealing with problems that appear to be spreading throughout the squad.
